Hon'ble Vivek Varma,J.
1.

Heard counsel for the applicants, Sri Jagdish Prasad Mishra, learned counsel for the opposite
party no.2 and learned A.G.A. for the State.

2.  The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the entire criminal proceedings of Criminal Case No. 275 of 2023 (State Vs. Chirag Bansal and others), arising out of Case Crime No.
395 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Jewar, District Gautam Budh Nagar, pending in the Court of Civil Judge (Jr. Div.)/Judicial Magistrate Jewar, District Gautam Budh Nagar as well as charge sheet no. 01/2022 dated 09.12.2022 and order dated 16.02.2023 on the basis of compromise.

sentences.text: It is stated that compromise deed had been filed by the parties before the learned trial court.
It is further stated that pursuant to the order passed by this Court, the parties appeared and the court concerned verified the aforesaid compromise vide order dated 12.05.2023.
Certified copy of the order dated 12.05.2023 is annexed as Annexure-SA-1 to the supplementary affidavit.

5. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicants that if the criminal prosecution is allowed to proceed it may create further complication in the otherwise normal relationship that is arising between the hitherto bitterly estranged couple and their families.
6. Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 does not dispute the submissions advanced by the counsel for the applicants or the correctness of the documents relied upon by him.

7. In view of the fact that the dispute appears to be purely of a personal nature being a matrimonial dispute that has been mutually settled between the parties, to their satisfaction, no useful purpose would be served in allowing such a prosecution to proceed any further.

8. Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in B.S.
Joshi v. State of Haryana, 2003(4) SCC 675, as well as Nikhil Merchant v. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, J.T., 2008 (9) SC 192, the proceedings of the aforesaid case are hereby set aside.
